info.title: RedSecTools API
info.description: Repository-only OpenAPI documentation for RedSecTools. This file is not served by the live application. It documents the current HTTP API, including auth requirements for main app, guest-link, extension, and admin routes. RedSecCal supports multi-day entry series with weekdays-only fan-out and series-level edit/delete. RedSecEngage includes full client, contact, opportunity, engagement, QA, team, activity, and cross-tool linking routes. RedSecReporter includes first-class proposals, proposal templates, and test-type write-ups alongside existing project, finding, design, and PDF generation routes.

UserSessionCookie.name: redsec_session
UserSessionCookie.description: Signed user session cookie created by POST /api/auth/login. Required for all authenticated API routes under /api (except public endpoints like survey response). The session encodes the user ID and is verified against server-side session storage. Sessions expire based on server configuration (default 24h, extended sessions up to 30 days with 'keep me signed in'). MFA-protected accounts require completing POST /api/auth/login/mfa before the session is promoted to fully authenticated.

GuestSessionCookie.name: redsec_guest
GuestSessionCookie.description: Signed guest cookie created by visiting /guest/{token}. Grants access only to paste creation (POST /api/paste) or share creation (POST /api/share), depending on the link scope. Guest sessions cannot access any other API routes.

ExtensionBearer.description: Bearer token returned by POST /api/ext/auth/login. Used by the Chrome extension API under /api/ext. Tokens expire based on server session TTL. Extension sessions have the same RBAC permissions as the linked user account but are separate from browser sessions.

AdminCookie.name: redsec_admin
AdminCookie.description: Signed admin session cookie created by POST /admin/login. Required for all routes under /admin/api. After initial bootstrap, admin API access also requires an active linked UserSessionCookie (redsec_session) — both cookies must be present. This two-step auth ensures admin actions are tied to a logged-in user session.

ivPassword.description: Base64 12-byte IV used by the password re-encryption layer when hasPassword is true.

salt.description: Base64 16-byte PBKDF2 salt when hasPassword is true.
